title: Choose PrepAhead's new look
question: Bolder hand, simple and definitive this time: no cute type, no drawn dishes. The dice dealt Concourse Board to lead. Pick one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Concourse Board
options.thesis: The one number that matters sits in flip cells and clacks over when a pre-order changes it.
options.viewport: Steel-grey page; tablet leads with TRAYS TO COOK 09 in flip cells, orders below as a plain ruled board; phone leads with your collection time in flip cells.
options.risk: Close to last round's boarding pass, and it reads transit before lunch.

raised.raise: Flip cells are reserved for one number per screen; everything else is plain type.
The order row being acted on lifts; the rest of the board dims.

options.label: Proof Sheet
options.lineage: monochrome product design: one neutral scale, one accent
options.thesis: Black and white, with green meaning only one thing: demand someone has already committed to.
materials: one green accent with one meaning
options.viewport: White page, near-black type; the tablet's 9 trays sits directly over its proof, a bar where the green slice is pre-ordered portions.
options.case: Beats the leader on both: it is exactly simple yet definitive, and every number shows its working, which is the project's argument.
options.risk: Without the green rule held strictly it slides into generic startup grey.

options.label: Grid Numerals
options.thesis: The numbers that matter are built from grid cells, on one yellow plane.
options.viewport: White sheet with a faint grid; tablet's 9 and the phone's 4821 code are built from squares on a yellow plane; everything else small and neutral.
options.case: Strongly definitive and simple; loses narrowly on clarity because the visible grid adds texture to reading.
options.risk: Can read as a design-school poster if the grid spreads past the number zones.

options.label: Line Map
options.thesis: Every order rides a line: placed, accepted, on shelf, collected, as stations.
options.viewport: Midnight header; stalls as stations NS01 to NS04 on one line; each order on the tablet shows its own four-station progress line.
options.case: Every NTU student reads a line map instantly; loses on simplicity because four line colours compete.
options.risk: Must not look like the real MRT map or its branding.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: a 1971 pocket timetable on a light table
options.thesis: Everything at one type size on raked glass slides.
options.viewport: Raked slides of orders lying across a goldenrod bed.
options.case: One type size forbids the one big number the stall needs; raked slides slow reading.
options.kept: Only one element per screen gets a reversed plate.
options.risk: Striking but slow to read at a counter.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Stalls as poster tiles in sideways rows; the focused one grows.
options.viewport: Rows of stall posters on a dark wall.
options.case: We have no dish artwork, and a dark poster wall is the opposite of simple.
options.kept: The row being acted on lifts and the rest dims.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard food-delivery app: white cards, dish photos, one brand colour.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar, category row, stall cards with photo, KPI tiles on the tablet.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every delivery app, and we have no real dish photos.
